probe_provenance: Every probe below was executed LIVE by warroom/fact_check against the running FalkorDB container gh-falkor (image falkordb/falkordb:v4.22.1, AF-9) via the FalkorDB client, with the exact Cypher recorded in warroom/deliberation-transcript.md. claims.claim: The algorithm procedures MENGER depends on exist in FalkorDB v4.22.1 — and the ones the first design assumed do NOT.

probe.evidence: algo.dijkstra and algo.SCC DO NOT EXIST. Real set re-derived live: AStar, BFS, HarmonicCentrality, MSF, SPpaths, SSpaths, WCC, betweenness, labelPropagation, maxFlow, pageRank. WORKAROUND (recorded, and already folded into PLAN.md + CONTRACT.md): the design was re-cut onto algo.SPpaths for weighted shortest path and algo.maxFlow for independence BEFORE forge wrote anything. Nothing in the frozen contract calls a non-existent procedure.

claims.claim: algo.SPpaths accepts a weight key, so reliability over -ln(trust) edges is computable.

probe.evidence: ONLY the key name 'weightProp' works. weightProperty / relationshipWeightProperty / costProperty are accepted SILENTLY and return HOP COUNT instead of the weighted total — no error is raised, so a wrong key yields a plausible wrong number. WORKAROUND: the exact key is pinned in CONTRACT.md and the measured weight 0.21072 is published as a BOOT ASSERTION by GET /health (AF-16) — a silent key regression returns 503 BOOT_ASSERTION_FAILED rather than a wrong headline.

claims.claim: algo.maxFlow's call signature supports the independence computation.

probe.evidence: algo.maxFlow({relationshipTypes:[exactly one], sourceNodes:[], targetNodes:[], capacityProperty:'cap'}) YIELD maxFlow, nodes. Constraint discovered live: relationshipTypes takes EXACTLY ONE type, not a list of several.

claims.claim: maxFlow over the provenance DAG counts VERTEX-disjoint origin chains (Menger's theorem) — the headline independence claim.

probe.target: gh-falkor — unit-capacity maxFlow on an echo graph vs an independent-sources graph
probe.evidence: maxFlow over unit-cap edges counts EDGE-disjoint paths, NOT vertex-disjoint — which is the wrong quantity: an echo through one shared source would have scored as independent. WORKAROUND, and the single most load-bearing design decision in the project: NODE-SPLIT the DAG (each vertex becomes in/out with a unit-capacity internal edge), which makes edge-disjoint == vertex-disjoint. Proven live after the split: echo graph -> 1, independent-sources graph -> 2. Both numbers are published as boot assertions (AF-16). Node-split is non-negotiable (DS-1) precisely because this probe failed without it.

claims.claim: maxFlow is fast enough at demo scale to sit in the POST /remember request path.

probe.evidence: 41ms cold / 11ms warm. Not the bottleneck; the admission decision can be synchronous.

claims.claim: GRAPH.RO_QUERY is a real server-side containment boundary for generated Cypher — the basis for calling a receipt replayable against an unmutated graph.

probe.target: gh-falkor — GRAPH.RO_QUERY with a CREATE and with a MATCH
probe.evidence: CREATE is REJECTED server-side; MATCH is allowed. Containment is enforced by the engine, not by client-side string inspection. Consequence pinned in the contract: all reads go through the Python client, because the TS client does not expose RO_QUERY (FalkorDB issue #408).

claims.claim: The engine version MENGER is built against is pinned and real.

probe.evidence: Pinned to v4.22.1 by explicit tag, not :latest. :latest currently resolves to 4.22.1 despite 6.0 release notes, and GraphRAG-SDK is broken on 6.0.x — so the pin is load-bearing, not cosmetic. All probes above ran against this exact image.
